content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.67) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., <0.33) or when sentiment shifts from positive to negative — model fails to adjust downward quickly.
- Forecast tends to lag in downward corrections — true price drops faster than model predicts, especially after strong sentiment spikes.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overcorrects or undercorrects — use recent 3-5 day mean as anchor for adjustment.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >75) — model often forecasts a peak and then overcorrects downward, missing the true trough.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to historical mean too quickly — adjust for longer-term trend persistence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent sentiment swings — dampen forecast if sentiment volatility >0.40 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is falling, model may misread sentiment as “bullish” and ignore bearish signals — reduce forecast by 5-10% in such cases.
